title: microbench-kvcache-tracing-proto
content:
Purpose
---
This is a working prototype spec for a lightweight microbenchmarking harness and regression detection flow focused on three risk areas in the serving runtime: kernel selection performance, scheduler behavior under mixed workloads, and KV-cache effectiveness for long-context workloads.

Scope and goals
- Quick, low-friction microbench harness that devs can run locally and CI can run nightly.
- Capture per-kernel and per-op timing, end-to-end latency distributions, and rich traces that correlate scheduling decisions with latency spikes.
- Provide deterministic workload generators for: tiny-chat (short seq), long-context completion (KV cache hit patterns), and mixed throughput burst test (many concurrent short requests).
- Automatic regression detection with tunable sensitivity and guided triage snippets for root cause (kernel change vs scheduler vs cache).

High-level architecture
- Harness driver (python CLI) spawns a local runtime instance or connects to a test cluster endpoint.
- Workload generator modules (JS/Python snippets) that produce token streams and prompt shapes.
- Trace collector: integrates with existing tracing hooks (op-level spans) and emits folded traces in JSON+protobuf-lite for analysis.
- Analyzer: lightweight rules engine that produces a regression report and suggested suspects.

Key measurements (per run)
- Per-token throughput (tokens/sec) by kernel and by layer
- Token-level p50/p95/p99 latency and tail skew across GPUs
- Scheduler metrics: task queue wait time, preemption count, fairness score (simple ratio), batching window distribution
- KV-cache metrics: hit rate per-prefix length, cache lookup latency, cache eviction churn
- Memory and memcpy times for each kernel variant

Microbench scenarios (initial set)
1) Kernel-isolation: single-stream, long-prefix generation to exercise attention kernel and KV cache. Sequence lengths: 512 -> 4096 (step). Assert: p50 per-token should not regress >7% across kernel changes.
2) Scheduler-stress: 1000 concurrent short requests (avg 30 tokens). Mix of priority levels (normal/cached/high). Measure queue wait and end-to-end percentiles.
3) Mixed-burst: background batch throughput (embeddings/long requests) with intermittent low-latency priority requests. Goal: validate latency SLO for priority path.
4) Cache-hit-gradient: generate synthetic prompts that share prefixes to vary cache hit rates (0%, 50%, 90%) and capture per-token speedups.

Trace format and required spans
- Root span: request_id, model_id, config (batching, quant, device)
- Scheduler->enqueue and ->dequeue spans with queue depth tag
- Kernel span(s): kernel_name, layer_id, input_shape, time_ns
- KV-cache: lookup span, hit boolean, serialized key_size
- Memcpy spans: host->device, device->host, type (pinned vs pageable)
- Fallback paths: model-variant-fallback span if triggered

Trace collection notes
- Use adaptive sampling in CI to keep trace size down: always capture full traces for failed runs or tail latency > threshold, sample 1% otherwise.
- Local dev runs default to full trace capture for easier debugging.

Regression detection heuristics
- Delta rules:
  - If p50 increases by > 7% AND p95 increases by > 10% -> flag as potential kernel or compile change
  - If queue_wait p50 increases by > 15% and kernel timings unchanged -> flag scheduler
  - If KV hit rate drops by > 10% causing >5% end-to-end slowdown -> flag data path/cache logic
- Cross-check suspects: correlate timestamps of new kernel/PR build vs regression window; present candidate PRs from linked CI builds.

Example local run and triage snippet (proto)
- Command: python harness.py run --profile kernel-isolation --model redwood/open-7b --device cuda:0 --trace out.trace.json
- ``Observations``: p50 token latency jumped from 24ms -> 38ms after PR#712. Per-layer kernel timings show Layer 10 attention kernel increased by 45% (memcpy also up 2x). Queue_wait unchanged. KV hit rate stable at 89%.
- ``Likely cause``: kernel change impacting attention perf (look at PR 712 kernel selection diff).

Baselines (examples to seed CI)
- open-7b, seq=1024, batch=1: baseline p50 24ms, p95 47ms, tokens/sec 420
- open-7b, seq=4096, batch=1, KV-hit=90%: baseline p50 48ms, p95 110ms, tokens/sec 120

CI integration plan
- Nightly job runs harness across 3 representative configs (small, med, long). Store metrics and traces in artifact store.
- Regression detector runs after each nightly; failures open JIRA with attached summary and top-correlated traces.
- On PR: quick smoke (unit microbench) runs in pre-merge; if smoke regresses beyond hard thresholds, block merge.

Repro steps for triage
1) Re-run harness with same seed and --fix-device to reproduce on same GPU type.
2) Enable full trace capture and attach out.trace.json to ticket.
3) Run kernel-compare tool (scripts/kernel-diff.sh) to produce per-op time deltas.
4) If scheduler suspected, enable queue debugging env var and re-run stress profile.

Open questions / risks
- Cost: storing full traces nightly is heavy. Need retention policy (30d full, 90d aggregated) + sampling.
- Determinism: stochastic schedulers and kernel selection heuristics may introduce noise. We need seeded RNG and stable build matrix for CI baselines.
- Cross-device variance: baselines must be per-GPU model (A10G vs H100 differences). Consider tagging baseline per device family.

Action items (next 6 weeks)
- Week 1: land harness CLI + kernel-isolation scenario (Ava + Samir)
- Week 2: add trace emitter & analyzer rules (Priya)
- Week 3: CI nightly job and artifact retention policy (Diego)
- Week 4-6: expand scenarios (scheduler stress + mixed-burst), iterate on heuristics, run against last 3 months of builds to seed baselines.

Notes to self (informal)
- Keep harness small — dev ergonomics > exhaustive coverage initially.
- Add small library of synthetic prompts for cache-hit-gradient, make them easy to tweak.
- FWIW: I saw odd memcpy jumps on H100 in local testing when quantization path changed; worth a targeted microprobe.

References and links
